subject: Coord: offboarding calendar + auto-renew exception language (MSA/Order Form)
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: ACME Procurement <procurement@acme.com>, Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Coordination: offboarding calendar + auto-renew exception language (MSA/Order Form)

Hi Sarah / ACME procurement team,

Quick note to align on the redlines we've proposed for term/renewal mechanics on the MSA + Order Form. Procurement asked for clear calendar mapping so finance and legal can lock billing and notice windows without back-and-forth. Attached are two artifacts: a marked-up Order Form (OrderForm_v4_redline.pdf) and an internal playbook for how we handle termination-for-convenience (TFC_playbook.docx).

High-level proposal (for clarity):
- Term: 12-month initial term, then successive 12-month renewals.
- Auto-renew: Order Form auto-renews for successive 12-month periods unless a party provides notice at least 60 days before the renewal effective date.
- Notice windows: standard 60-day window on Order Forms; for enterprise customers we can support 90-day where required by procurement but that should be scoped as an exception and requires revenue ops confirmation.
- Termination for convenience: mutual TFC allowed with a 60-day notice and a termination fee equal to 25% of remaining committed monthly recurring revenue (MRR) if terminated inside the first 6 months of a renewal period. After month 6, refundable credit only for pre-paid unused services.

Requests from our side:
1) Confirm whether ACME can accept a mutual 60-day opt-out as standard, or if you need 90 days as the default for all orders.
2) If you require longer notices, confirm whether ACME will accept a tiered notice (90 days for >$1M TCV deals, 60 days otherwise).
3) Procurement: please provide your primary procurement contact and the date by which you need the signed Order Form to hit your fiscal quarter close so we can prioritize DocuSign routing.

Ben / Karthik — looping you in so we can finalize language and prepare a DocuSign envelope for ACME if they confirm. I want to avoid multiple redlines; if procurement requests 90 days we should capture that as a single, clear exception in the MSA rather than ad-hoc order form edits.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Enterprise Contracts | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachments: OrderForm_v4_redline.pdf (redline), TFC_playbook.docx (internal guidance)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, ACME Procurement <procurement@acme.com>, Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>

Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Coordination: offboarding calendar + auto-renew exception language (MSA/Order Form)

Thanks Kim — good summary. A few quick commercial points from my side:

- From Sales' POV we prefer a 60-day standard notice; it keeps renewals predictable for both sides and maps cleanly to monthly billing cycles.
- If ACME needs 90 days, we can accept it but would like that to be a negotiated term tied to deal TCV (e.g., 90 days for >$1M TCV). Otherwise we risk too many bespoke exceptions.
- On the TFC fee: 25% of remaining committed MRR in the first 6 months of a renewal is reasonable. For smaller pilots (pilot PO < $50k) propose we waive the fee but require a 30-day notice only.

Action items for our side:
- Karthik: can you prepare two alternate redline passages for the MSA: (A) mutual 60-day standard; (B) mutual 90-day default for >$1M deals + 60 otherwise.
- Kim: if procurement confirms a required date to sign, I will prioritize the ACME opportunity and loop revenue ops to reserve the renewal bucket.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Thanks Kimberly — appreciate the clear summary and attachments. A couple of points from procurement: 

1) ACME prefers 90-day notice as our standard internal policy. We can accept 60 days for pilot projects under $100k, but for any production/order-level deal we need 90 days.
2) Regarding TFC fees: procurement will need an explicit formula tied to remaining committed spend and confirmation that any termination credit is applied to pre-paid invoices only. We can't accept open-ended credits.
3) Can Redwood provide a single DocuSign envelope for the Order Form + MSA amendment so our legal and procurement teams can sign in one flow?

If you can send the DocuSign link and updated redline that reflects 90-day default with a 60-day carveout for pilots, we will review internally and aim to respond within 72 hours. Our target is to have the order signed before ACME's quarter close on 2026-12-20.

Subject: Final proposed language + next steps (MSA redline options)

Kim / Ben / Sarah — thanks for the fast turnaround. I've drafted two alternative clauses and attached them to this thread (see OrderForm_v4_redline.pdf). Summary below — this is the wording I recommend we push to ACME to minimize iteration: 

Option 1 (recommended, clean):
- Auto-renew: "This Order Form will automatically renew for successive twelve (12) month periods unless either party provides written notice of non-renewal at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term."
- TFC: "Either party may terminate this Order Form for convenience upon sixty (60) days written notice to the other party. If termination occurs within the first six (6) months of any renewal period, the terminating party will owe a termination fee equal to twenty-five percent (25%) of the remaining committed Monthly Recurring Revenue under the then-current Order Form; thereafter, Redwood will issue a pro rata credit for any prepaid, unused services."

Option 2 (procurement-friendly):
- Identical to Option 1 except: default notice = ninety (90) days for Order Forms with total contract value (TCV) equal to or greater than One Million U.S. Dollars (USD $1,000,000); sixty (60) days for all other Order Forms. Pilot orders under $100k get a 30-day notice with no termination fee.

Next steps: 
- Kim: please confirm which option we present in the DocuSign envelope. I recommend Option 2 only if ACME confirms they require 90 days across the board; otherwise present Option 1 and offer Option 2 as a visible exception (via checkbox in the DocuSign order).
- Ben: I will prepare the redline and a single DocuSign envelope that includes the MSA amendment + Order Form. I will also flag HubSpot deal HUB-57931 and include a comment that we have the 12/20 quarter-close target.
- Sarah / ACME team: if you confirm Option 2 as required, please indicate whether the >$1M threshold is acceptable or whether you need blanket 90 days for all orders.

I will also add a short runbook in the shared Drive (link above) that operations can follow to map renewal dates to billing cycles and to automate notice reminders 75 days before renewal for 90-day deals (and 45 days for 60-day deals).

Thanks all — I will send the DocuSign link Monday morning PST unless you ask for an earlier send.

Karthik Iyer
Principal Contracts Counsel | Redwood Inference
